clue.text: In possession of Staff? Then I've lost it

definitions.text: In possession of Staff? Then I've lost it

parts.words: In possession of Staff? Then I've lost it
parts.note: a Staff is a Staffordshire bull terrier, so having one means owning a hound; to have lost it is to be mad, or barking, yourself

explanation.surface: Someone with employees to call on finds they have snapped under the strain anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees, but it is the dog breed; 'lost it' means gone mad, i.e. barking. Together they give the saying 'Why keep a dog and bark yourself?', for doing a job you pay someone else to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb mocks anyone who pays a helper and then does the helper's work personally.

clue.text: Arrange, e.g., to do Tchaikovsky Night in full clobber?

indicators.note: to arrange music is to rework it, so the letters of the following words are reordered

parts.words: e.g., to do Tchaikovsky Night in full
parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A musician is asked to score an evening of Tchaikovsky, played in full costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobber' looks like British slang for clothes, as in full clobber, but here it is the verb to beat soundly. The anagram uses all 28 letters from 'e.g.' to 'full'.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber someone is to hit them very hard, which the idiom describes as a severe beating.

clue.text: First and third notes appended to cheese snack

indicators.note: appended to means these letters are added after the cheese

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese
A is the first note of the scale from A to G, and ME (mi) the third of doh-ray-me

explanation.surface: A cheese plate topped off with a couple of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Edamame are young soya beans in the pod, served salted as a snack or appetiser.

clue.text: Harmless illegal pot one has being seized

indicators.note: seized means gripped, so this word is held between the other parts

parts.note: in snooker an in-off, the cue ball going into a pocket off another ball, is a foul shot
I've is short for I have, and I is one
ens is the Latin and philosophical word for being or existence

explanation.surface: Someone caught holding cannabis protests it is harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' tempts toward cannabis, but here it is a snooker shot; 'being' is the Latin philosophers' word, a crossword convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inoffensive gives no offence and causes no harm.

clue.text: Passage hitched to stern of tug boat

indicators.note: hitched to means joined on behind
the stern is a ship's rear, so the last letter of the word

parts.note: an alley is a narrow passage between buildings

explanation.surface: A boat's passageway is tied to the back of a tugboat for towing.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is a low, oared ship, as well as a ship's kitchen.

clue.text: Lad's come to represent the victim of indefinite suspension!

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged to represent, or stand for, another name

parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A boy arrives to stand in for someone left hanging indefinitely.
explanation.walkthrough: Damocles sat beneath a sword hung by a single hair, a suspension with no set end.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the courtier sat under a sword hanging by one horsehair, never knowing when it might fall.

clue.text: Censor one of the jokes?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to silence or censor

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks whether a censor is himself a joke; each half is a separate meaning of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for suppressing speech and as a noun for a comedian's quip.

clue.text: So not entirely shunning orders?

indicators.note: orders here means arrangements, so the letters are put in a new order
not entirely means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A wry question: is someone half-heartedly turning their back on religious orders?
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' doubles as religious orders in the whole-clue reading; SHUNNIN, from 'shunning' less its last letter, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nunlike in manner keeps close to holy orders rather than wholly shunning them.

clue.text: See 1
Enjoying continued success with the vote?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: enjoying a winning streak
second meaning: listed on an electoral roll, so entitled to vote

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: your name is on the electoral roll, the register of voters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a run of successes, and literally a name entered on the register of voters.

clue.text: Red setter, perhaps, adopted by old lady

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for one's mother, an old lady in slang
a setting agent, such as pectin, makes things set

explanation.surface: An elderly woman takes in a red setter dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red setter' reads as the dog breed, but 'Red' is the definition and the setter is a setting agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red colour, named after a battle in Italy.

clue.text: This bird offers very little strokeability!

indicators.note: only a small part of the word is given up, so the letters lie within it

explanation.surface: A joke that this bird barely lets anyone pet it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strokeability' is a made-up word, and only three of its letters are offered up.
explanation.definitionFit: The kea is a large mountain parrot of New Zealand.

clue.text: A1 ____ ____ from France is thick? That's wrong

definitions.text: A1 ____ ____ from France is thick? That's wrong

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters are jumbled, here with A1's letters added to the answer

parts.note: A1 is read as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: Someone protests that saying an excellent loaf from France is thick is a slander.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A1 plus the answer, rearranged, give FRANCE IS THICK; so the A1 loaf from France is thick, which the clue says is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is the long thin loaf of France, the opposite of thick.

clue.text: Wheels turn inside core for cooling, I'd say

parts.note: a stretch is a turn, or term, served inside prison

indicators.note: the core is the centre, so the middle letter of the word

parts.note: IMO is the texting abbreviation for in my opinion

explanation.surface: Wheels revolve around a central cooling element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' is slang for a car; 'turn' is a spell in jail, not a rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch limo is a lengthened luxury car, and wheels is slang for a vehicle.

clue.text: Farrier's work donating spades for gardener's?

definitions.note: short for gardener's work, matching Farrier's work

indicators.note: donating means giving away, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: a farrier's job is shoeing horses
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A blacksmith gives away spades to a gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'work' after 'Farrier's' is understood after 'gardener's' too.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking soil and weeding with a hoe is routine garden labour.

clue.text: Home victory is without fray

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go round the other

parts.note: a win is a victory
Earth is our home planet

explanation.surface: A home win was achieved without any fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking; 'fray' is the verb, not a scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth that frays becomes worn and threadbare at the edges.

clue.text: "Sign Rocky for good", one croaks

parts.note: the Bull is Taurus, a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: rocky means shaky or unsteady, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxing promoter's slogan urges signing the fighter Rocky for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' points to the boxer, but it shuffles 'for'; 'croaks' sounds like dying, but is a frog's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfrog is a large frog with a deep, booming croak.

clue.text: Back in the air with difficulty, landed about one minute from here?

indicators.note: about means going around, so these letters enclose the rest

parts.note: lit is the past tense of light, to land or settle

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: up means aloft, in the air
ill means badly, with difficulty, as in ill afford

explanation.surface: Coming down awkwardly, a flier lands about a minute's distance from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one minute' is not sixty seconds but one tiny person: the land of the six-inch Lilliputians. LLIPU sits inside LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels the island's inhabitants are all tiny people.

clue.text: Ladies' facilities? In one, a lady

parts.note: a lav is a lavatory, here the ladies'
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman is spotted in the ladies' toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' facilities' is a lav in British slang; the last word of the clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavinia is a woman's name, the wife of Aeneas in Roman legend.

clue.text: Officer hacks around cement on walls

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to hack is to cut
CO is short for commanding officer

explanation.surface: An officer chips away at the mortar on walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a plaster or render applied to the outside of buildings.

clue.text: The Boston Tea Party, maybe a vehicle for war?

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
a riot is a wild party, and the Boston event was a riot about tea

explanation.surface: Asking whether the Boston Tea Party was really a warlike vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boston Tea Party, a 1773 protest in which tea was dumped in the harbour, is literally a tea riot: CHA RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot was a two-wheeled horse-drawn cart used in ancient battles.

clue.text: Driver caught empty panel-truck?

indicators.note: caught by the ear, so the letters are heard as a word

parts.note: emptying panel-truck leaves its outer letters P and K, which are said aloud as pee-kay

explanation.surface: A driver is caught in an empty delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: P and K, said aloud, sound like Nelson Piquet, the Brazilian Formula One champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Piquet was a racing driver who won three Formula One world championships.

clue.text: Between 6 and 8, briefly compete with Netherlands actress

indicators.note: between means these letters sit inside the other pair

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: eight spelt out
to vie is to compete
NL is the country code for the Netherlands

explanation.surface: An actress in a quick scrap with the Dutch for the time between six and eight.
explanation.walkthrough: The figures 6 and 8 read like times of day, but they are numbers turned into letters: one as a Roman numeral, the other spelt out and cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivien Leigh was the British film star who played Scarlett O'Hara in Gone with the Wind.

clue.text: Cashier's unlimited state contributions

indicators.note: without limits, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: taxes are payments to the state

explanation.surface: A bank teller's losses are put down to the government's tax take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' is not the bank clerk but the verb, to dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier someone is to dismiss them, especially from the armed forces, which is to sack or fire.

clue.text: One doesn't take drugs (one's run out)

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone abstinent who has run out of supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hides the fodder: 'one's run' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who abstains entirely from narcotics is one who never uses them.

clue.text: The sun this large?

parts.note: so means to this extent, as in this big, so big
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Is the sun as big as this?
explanation.definitionFit: Sol is the Latin name for the sun, used in astronomy.

clue.text: Make a single confirmation of peacekeepers' ID tab?

parts.note: it is UN, the United Nations, said in the reverse order UN IT IS
E stands for ecstasy, taken as a tab or pill

explanation.surface: Checking whether a peacekeeper's identity label confirms their unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'UN? It is' confirms that the peacekeepers are United Nations troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To unitise is to combine separate parts into one whole unit.

clue.text: See 1
